bull.b: The shift to meaningful profitability and strong reported margins improves Protalix’s ability to fund operations and development internally. If commercial product economics remain favorable, this earnings base can provide greater resilience and support continued investment in the pipeline.

A debt-free balance sheet with substantial liquid resources gives Protalix flexibility to advance clinical programs, support commercialization and absorb operating variability without immediate financing pressure. This strengthens resilience while reducing interest burden and refinancing exposure.

Product sales growth combined with additional geographic and dosing approvals can broaden Elfabrio’s durable commercial reach. Regulatory progress may improve patient access and adoption, strengthening the product’s contribution to revenue and supporting Protalix’s position in Fabry disease.

bear.b: Dependence on Chiesi and uneven purchasing can make reported revenue difficult to forecast even when underlying demand is stable. This concentration increases the company’s exposure to partner inventory decisions and may create recurring volatility in sales, cash generation and resource planning.

The large milestone boosted near-term revenue but may not recur, making current growth rates and profitability less representative of ongoing product economics. Future performance will therefore depend more heavily on recurring Elfabrio sales and continued commercial execution.

The observed anti-drug antibody incidence could complicate dose selection, tolerability and the program’s progression toward Phase 3. Until efficacy and immunogenicity are resolved, PRX-115 carries meaningful development uncertainty that may affect timing, investment needs and commercial positioning.
